units.title: Intro to HTML
units.description: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard markup language for creating web pages. It describes the structure of a web page using elements represented by tags.

units.title: Text Formatting
units.description: HTML provides tags to format text. <b> makes text bold, <i> makes it italic. <strong> and <em> convey semantic importance.

units.title: Lists & Links
units.description: Lists organizes data. <ul> is unordered (bullets), <ol> is ordered (numbers). <a> creates hyperlinks.

units.title: Images & Media
units.description: Images are embedded with the tag. It is empty and contains attributes only. "src" specifies the path, "alt" provides text for screen readers.

units.title: Intro to CSS
units.description: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) formats the layout of a webpage. You can control color, font, size, and spacing.

units.title: CSS Selectors
units.description: Selectors allow you to select and manipulate HTML elements. Common ones are Element, ID, and Class selectors.

units.title: Box Model
units.description: All HTML elements can be considered as boxes. The Box Model wraps content with Margins, Borders, Padding, and Content.

units.title: Fonts & Text
units.description: CSS offers powerful text styling. You can change the font family, size, weight, alignment, and decoration.

units.title: Flexbox
units.description: Flexbox is a layout module used to arrange items in rows or columns without floats. It creates flexible responsive layouts.

units.title: CSS Grid
units.description: CSS Grid Layout is a 2-dimensional system, handling both columns and rows. It is perfect for page-wide layouts.

units.title: Responsive Design
units.description: Responsive Web Design makes web pages render well on all devices. Media queries (@media) allow you to apply different styles for different screen sizes.

units.title: Advanced Forms
units.description: Forms allow user input. <input> has many types like text, password, checkbox, radio, date. <select> makes dropdowns.

units.title: Semantic HTML
units.description: Semantic elements clearly describe their meaning to both the browser and the developer. Examples: <header>, <footer>, <article>, <section>.
